brief: GS's weekly roundup frames low risk appetite into year-end against weak hedge fund performance: at midday Oct 30, Fundamental L/S managers were down 1.2% on the day and 3.6% MTD (TMT funds -12.6% MTD, YTD cut to +5.1%), while Systematic managers (-0.6% day, -3.5% MTD, +16% YTD) tracked their first negative month of 2026. On mega-cap tech earnings, the debate centers on who captures AI investment returns and how the cycle gets financed; capex-discipline risk from financing constraints is not yet visible in spending intentions, and Sheridan stays constructive on AMZN post-print on constrained AWS capacity and margin expansion. For midterms, GS argues which policy debates (ACA subsidies, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending, corporate tax) gain momentum matters more than the outcome itself; near-term earnings look insulated either way, but Corporate Tax is a valuation risk beyond 2029. Hatzius sees 2027 growth downside if higher DM yields (~100bp since early 2026) persist, subtracting ~0.6% from GDP, and expects the AI growth impulse to have peaked in late 2026/early 2027. Rising debt costs favor Quality over a systemic credit event.
